newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's May CPI +0.5 pct vs +0.7 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Israel's May CPI +0.5 pct vs +0.7 pct in April.

text.p: The Central Bureau of Statistics issued the following economic indicator on Sunday:
ISRAEL CONSUMER PRICES May 97 Apr 97 May 96
Note: To compare previous indices based on 1987=100.0, multiply indices from January 1994 by 2.421.
The May index came in well under analysts' expectations, which were for 0.7 to 0.9 percent. The wholesale price index rose 0.3 percent.
The low CPI was due mainly to an 0.6 percent decline in housing prices, which offset big seasonal rises in fresh produce prices of 1.2 percent and clothing of 4.8 percent, the bureau said.

Market analysts said the CPI was very good news but were mixed on whether the Bank of Israel would respond by cutting rates later this month. The central bank is due to announce interest rates next Monday.

"The May CPI figure was very surprising and well below expectations, mainly because of the housing price index," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities. "We expect a 0.5 percentage point cut in interest rates for July."
He said he expected the market to rally "aggressively" on Monday. "All things being equal, the market will show a lot of strength tomorrow," he said.
But some traders were still unsure of the interest rate cut.

"The CPI was a surprise, but I don't know if (Bank of Israel Governor Jacob) Frenkel will lower interest rates at the end of the month. Maybe if it is part of a package deal. For sure now chances are better that he will do so. But Frenkel generally hurries more to raise rates than to lower them," said Doron Tsur of Sahar Securities.
Nevertheless, he said, the the market would react very positively to the news on Monday.
